title: Jonah and the Letters
premise: Hazel Coldharbour, a wedding planner whose own engagement ended in scandal seven years ago, has built a careful life of small safe steps: a struggling bakery, a rented flat, and a policy of never planning his own happy ending. When his mother summons him to the family's fortieth anniversary reunion, he hires Jonah Reyes—a charming stranger from the flower stall next door—to pose as his boyfriend for one weekend. But the fake date feels too real by dessert, and Jonah's warmth cracks open everything Hazel buried. As the bakery lease deadline looms and Jonah's own secrets surface in a box of unsent letters, Hazel must choose between staying invisible and risking the whole heart. In the end, Hazel signs the lease on a new shop with Jonah as partner, plans one last wedding—his sister's—and finally writes a letter of his own: a proposal.
about_author: Beatrix Pemberton is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent a decade behind the scenes of other people's weddings before turning to fiction. She writes love stories about people who are better at arranging happiness than claiming it.

chapters.title: The Cake That Never Got Cut
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Seven years after walking out of his own reception, Hazel ices someone else's wedding cake at 3 a.m., refusing a commission to plan full weddings. Emotional beat: grief disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Flowers Next Door
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The florist's lease next door changes hands; Jonah Reyes arrives with peonies and relentless cheer. Their banter over shared loading-dock space sparks something Hazel refuses to name. Beat: reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A gilt-edged invitation arrives: his parents' ruby anniversary reunion, plus news that his sister Priya is engaged—and expects Hazel to bring 'someone.' Beat: dread tightening around old wounds.

chapters.title: A Transactional Proposal
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah, broke and behind on rent, overhears Hazel rehearsing excuses and offers himself as a fake boyfriend—for a fee. He tells himself it's just business. Beat: opportunism masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. Over coffee, they draft rules: no real names of exes, no touching unless required, no falling. The handshake lingers too long. Beat: comedy undercut by mutual awareness.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. First test run: dinner with Priya, who sees through nothing and everything. Jonah charms the table; Hazel watches him and forgets his lines. Beat: the fake starting to feel load-bearing.

chapters.title: The Lease Letter
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah finds an eviction notice tucked under Hazel's door—sixty days on the bakery lease. He says nothing, filing it away like a secret. Beat: guilt's first seed.

chapters.title: Packing for Pretend
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Shopping for the reunion weekend, Hazel realizes he owns nothing that isn't armor. Jonah picks out a soft blue shirt Hazel would never choose. Beat: vulnerability by proxy.

chapters.title: Arrival at Coldharbour House
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The family estate swallows them whole: cousins, aunts, and Hazel's father's appraising stare. Jonah's hand finds his without prompting. Beat: terror and unexpected steadiness.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At dessert, Hazel's aunt asks how they met, and Jonah improvises a story so tender it silences the room—including Hazel. Beat: the lie becomes truer than intended.

chapters.title: The Garden Confession
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Midnight in the garden, Hazel almost tells the truth about his broken engagement. Jonah stops him gently: 'You don't owe anyone your scars this weekend.' Beat: intimacy without exposure.

chapters.title: Mother Knows
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel's mother corners him, not about the fake boyfriend but about the bakery: 'You always loved small things you could control.' Beat: maternal insight as wound.

chapters.title: Sunday Breakfast Lie
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah watches the Coldharbours' quiet cruelties and recognizes his own family's patterns. He defends Hazel to his father—off-script. Beat: loyalty crossing contractual lines.

chapters.title: Driving Home in Silence
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The drive back is charged with everything unsaid. They agree, stiffly, that the job is done. Neither believes it. Beat: denial's last stand.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wants Everything
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A high-profile bride demands Hazel plan her wedding personally—the biggest commission of his career, due exactly when the lease expires. Beat: opportunity as trap.

chapters.title: Jonah's Box of Letters
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Alone, Jonah unpacks a shoebox of unsent letters to his late brother, revealing why he drifts through cities and never stays. Beat: hidden depth, mirrored avoidance.

chapters.title: Accidental Date
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A supplier mix-up strands them at a night market sharing dumplings. No audience, no contract—just laughter. Hazel catches himself reaching for Jonah's hand. Beat: want acknowledged, then fled.

chapters.title: Priya's Request
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya asks Hazel to plan her wedding, then adds: 'Bring Jonah. Real or not, he makes you brave.' Beat: sisterly truth-telling.

chapters.title: The Almost Kiss
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Late-night cake tasting, frosting on Jonah's thumb, faces inches apart—interrupted by a phone call from the reunion committee: another family event demands their return. Beat: suspended desire.

chapters.title: Second Weekend, Fewer Rules
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Back at Coldharbour House, the pretense is thinner. They share a room by 'accident' and talk until dawn about everything except themselves. Beat: closeness as confession.

chapters.title: The Father's Offer
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel's father offers to buy the bakery building—if Hazel quits weddings entirely and joins the family firm. Beat: survival dangled at the price of identity.

chapters.title: Jonah Says Yes Too Fast
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah urges Hazel to take the deal, hiding that he's already been offered a year-long floral residency abroad. Beat: fear dressed as pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Fight About Small Steps
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The argument erupts: Hazel accuses Jonah of never staying; Jonah accuses Hazel of never starting. Old wounds weaponized. Beat: rupture.

chapters.title: Sixty Days Become Thirty
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The landlord serves final notice. Hazel, alone, drafts an acceptance email to his father and cannot press send. Beat: rock bottom of self-betrayal.

chapters.title: The Letters Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah reads one brother-letter aloud to an empty shop and realizes Hazel is the first person he's wanted to stay for. Beat: turning point inward.

chapters.title: The Bride's Crisis
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. His flagship client's wedding implodes—venue flooded, groom gone. Hazel must rebuild it in nine days or lose everything. Beat: crisis as crucible.

chapters.title: Asking for Help
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. For the first time in seven years, Hazel asks Jonah for help—not as a hire, but as a partner. Jonah says yes before the sentence ends. Beat: humility as bridge.

chapters.title: Nine Days of Rebuilding
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Montage chapter: flowers, rewired lights, 4 a.m. sugar work. They move around each other like they've done this forever. Beat: partnership made visible.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Works
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The rescued wedding is beautiful. Watching the vows, Hazel realizes he's been planning everyone's forever except his own. Beat: epiphany amid celebration.

chapters.title: Jonah's Departure Date
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The residency confirmation arrives: flights in two weeks. Jonah hides the email, hating himself. Beat: secret as ticking bomb.

chapters.title: Discovery
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel finds the printed itinerary in Jonah's van—and the eviction notice Jonah never mentioned. Betrayal stacks on betrayal. Beat: devastation.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Rain
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The fight in the storm: 'You were going to leave.' 'You were going to disappear into your father's house!' Both true. Jonah walks. Beat: climax of loss.

chapters.title: The Empty Shop
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Jonah's flower stall stands gutted. Hazel bakes all night, then finally opens his father's email and types 'No.' Beat: choosing self over safety.

chapters.title: Reading the Last Letter
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. On the plane's tarmac, Jonah reads his brother's final letter: 'Go home, even if home is a person.' He deplanes. Beat: redemption's pivot.

chapters.title: The Lease Signing
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel signs a new lease using his savings and the commission fee—keeping the bakery, keeping the dream, alone. It's enough, he tells himself. Beat: independence with an ache.

chapters.title: Peonies on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Dawn: a bucket of peonies on the bakery step, and Jonah, soaked from walking from the station. No speech—just 'I'm bad at staying. Teach me.' Beat: the grand gesture made humble.

chapters.title: Priya's Wedding Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Hazel plans his sister's wedding flawlessly; Jonah runs the flowers. During the vows, Hazel slips a ring box into Jonah's pocket—unspoken promise. Beat: joy earned collectively.

chapters.title: The Letter Hazel Writes
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel finally writes a letter of his own—to himself, seven years ago—then burns it in the bakery oven and feels lighter. Beat: release of the past.

chapters.title: The Question
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. On the beach where they once pretended, Jonah reads Hazel a letter he wrote during the flight home, ending with a question. Hazel answers yes before he finishes. Beat: climax of love.

chapters.title: Two Names on the Lease
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, epilogue. One year later: the bakery and flower shop share a wall and a lease with both their names. Hazel plans one more wedding—his own—and believes in it completely. Beat: wholeness.
